claims.text: Introduction/Context
Zotatifin, a clinical eIF4A inhibitor, was tested on 22Rv1 prostate cancer cell xenografts in vivo.
After 6 h treatment, Ribo-seq identified 554 transcripts downregulated at the translational level (FDR < 0.01, log2FC ≤ −0.3) and MS detected 339 proteins downregulated (p < 0.05, log2FC ≤ −0.2).
Using less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 & log2FC < 0; MS p < 0.05 & log2FC < 0), 108 genes were concordantly downregulated at both levels.
Keywords
• Translation initiation
• eIF4A inhibition
• Hypoxia signaling
• PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway

Comparisons
• AR, HIF1A and PDCD4 were downregulated in both Ribo-seq (FDR < 1e-6 for AR; PDCD4 in multiple hallmarks) and MS (p < 0.01), highlighting robust cross-modality hits.
• PI3K pathway components (PIK3CA/GSK3B) appear in GSEA, ORA and leading-edge gene tables, underscoring strong attenuation of proliferative signaling.
• Cell-cycle factors (TPX2, RAD21) map to G2/M and mitotic spindle terms, reflecting a halt in proliferation.
Implications
Zotatifin dampens eIF4A-dependent translation of key oncogenic drivers (AR, HIF1A, PDCD4), leading to down-regulation of hypoxia adaptation, androgen signaling and cell-cycle progression.
Suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR and G2/M pathways may underlie its antitumor efficacy in PCa.
